:::{#exm-fisher-kl-poisson}
#### Curvature of the divergence for Poisson data

For one observation $X \sim \Pois(\rate_0)$,
$\log \p(x \mid \rate) = x \log \rate - \rate - \log x!$, so

$$
\ba
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\rate)
&= \Expp_{\rate_0}\sb{X \log \frac{\rate_0}{\rate} - \rate_0 + \rate}\\
&= \rate_0 \log \frac{\rate_0}{\rate} - \rate_0 + \rate.
\ea
$$

Differentiating twice with respect to $\rate$ gives
$D_{\mathrm{KL}}'(\rate) = 1 - \rate_0 / \rate$
and $D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\rate) = \rate_0 / \rate^2$,
so $D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\rate_0) = 1/\rate_0$,
which is the expected information of one observation (@exm-information-poisson).
A numerical second difference of the divergence,
summed directly over the Poisson probabilities, agrees:

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
rate_0 <- 3
kl_div <- function(rate) {
  x <- 0:200
  sum(dpois(x, rate_0) * (dpois(x, rate_0, log = TRUE) - dpois(x, rate, log = TRUE)))
}
h <- 1e-3
c(
  second_difference = (kl_div(rate_0 + h) - 2 * kl_div(rate_0) + kl_div(rate_0 - h)) / h^2,
  expected_information = 1 / rate_0
)
```

:::
